The proposed technique combines the finite element method to formulate the fields within the cavity region and the boundary integral approach to represent the fields above the ground plane.
The method is applicable to cavities of arbitrary shape and material fillings, unlike traditional approaches that require knowledge of the cavity's Green's function.
The resulting system has a partly full and partly sparse, as well as symmetric and banded matrix, which can be solved efficiently using special algorithms.
The penalty term is used to implicitly satisfy the divergence conditions on the electric and magnetic fields, which helps to remove the spurious modes that can appear in finite element solutions.
The proposed formulation was found to be more computationally efficient than traditional formulations, such as the mode matching and moment method/modal approaches.

For the data in Figure 3, the proposed method took less than one minute on an Apollo DN10000, compared to five minutes on a Cray XMP-48 for the mode matching technique and two minutes on an Apollo DN10000 for the moment method/modal approach.
The proposed method is applicable to cavities filled with inhomogeneous material, whereas traditional approaches are not.
The method can treat arbitrary shape cavities by employing an appropriate mesh generation algorithm.

The basis functions used in the finite element discretization may not accurately represent the field singularities near sharp perfectly conducting edges, which can lead to errors in the calculated field distribution.
The penalty factor in the finite element formulation was found to have a small effect on the RCS pattern in most cases.
The data in Figure 2 show the distinct behavior of the aperture field associated with the cavity-backed structure, compared to that of a transmitting aperture.
The results in Figure 3 show excellent agreement between the proposed method and the moment method/modal approach, except at the point (φ = 90°) for θ = 90°.

The proposed formulation and the moment method/modal approach show excellent agreement for the backscatter RCS of a material-filled cavity, as shown in Figure 5.
The proposed formulation can handle cavities filled with multilayer material, which is not possible with traditional approaches, as demonstrated in Figure 6.
